source: Well. That's a trick, ey?
Normally I'd have ol' Finnegan here throw you over 'is shoulder and be on with it, but...
Tell you wot. If you won't come to O'Malley's vessel, we'll take over yer beaten old ship for ourselves.
We'll never swear allegiance to some Pirate Queen, nor serve under you.
Yes! I don't like being loyal to things! Pirates included!
My tender ladies, you've no choice in the matter. Starting today, I'm yer captain.
Name's Grace O'Malley, though you can call me 'evil salty bitch' if it makes yeh feel any better.
I and my men will be taking the captain's bunk, effective immediately.
And what are we to do, exactly? We were bound for England—
I don't give a horse's ass what yeh do or where yeh were bound. So make of that what yeh will.
...Now, if you'll excuse me, I'll be chartin' a new course.
...You shouldn't have done that, Hamlet.
Neither should I have slain your father. What's done is done.
Too late now. What's done is done.
Ophelia. May I speak to you alone?
That's a tall order on a cramped ship.
...Perhaps the forecastle deck?
The what?
The forecastle deck. The one near the bow.
You've scarcely been on a sailing vessel—if ever. How do you know that?
Well, I read, for one.
The time has come to discuss our deliverance back to shore.
A mutiny, you mean.
Yes. Are you... is that... amenable to you?
It's going to happen regardless. I'll be ready.
(What's gotten into her?)
We must rise up against the captain and take her by surprise.
And then do what, exactly?
We're utterly surrounded, and outnumbered. We've no weapons of any kind. I can't bear a sword. Uncertain about Rosie and Guilda.
There are still men loyal to us aboard. And I've a plan, besides.
Soon, the good captain will need to sleep—and at that point, she'll be unarmed.
Meanwhile, her lieutenant keeps the night watch. If he can be incapacitated, leaving her with no warning...
...Then we rush her?
...But... that woman didn't come here alone. Her first ship is fully manned and sails ahead of us. How will we return to Denmark once we've captured the ship?
That's just it. We don't have to return to Denmark. Merely run close enough to her shores that Grace's men dare not pursue us longer.
Without their leader's signal, they may be slow to react. I hate to admit this, but we might have the merest chance, if the wind favors us.
I'm glad I have your faith.
This plan of mine... there's a contingency built within it.
Ought I to be afraid?
Ophelia—if it should come to the worst of this matter, and Rosie and Guilda are captured...
...I've every intent of leaving them to Grace's sword.
You'd... let them die?
...Something happened. I don't want to discuss it. Not yet.
They're loyal to my uncle. He fills their pockets with coin, and they've spied on me in return.
In some ways, I'm merely their source of income. Whatever friendship we once had... it's... changed.
I should have realized they'd only look after themselves, and each other. It's always been that way, deep down.
You and I are the only ones who matter in this horrible, ugly world. And I'd sooner you live than I.
...Hamlet, I think your priorities may be misplaced, if keeping me alive is your goal.
What? Why wouldn't it be?
Never mind it. Let's put this plan to action and see what happens.
After they lied to me, nearly costing me my life...
You think me a fool?
Not quite. You see, there's someone else who wanted Hamlet dead.
The King!
Oh, I know all about it, loves.
I don' have much in th'way of integrity, but I do have a code o' sorts.
An' that code stipulates that friends don't betray friends.
That letter you bore... I canna' allow you to pollute any shore ever again.
... I should have known it would come to this.
And to think I thought it might go better this time.
Now. You.
Do I have to worry about you overthrowing me, too?
Even if I wanted to, I've no means to do so.
I'll be returned to the past soon regardless. This fate means little to me.
Hmph. Sounds like a lot of poetic nothing.
All of you have lied to me, nearly costing me my life...
...For the dog who would throw his companions to the depths, I've a special punishment.
Y-you mean—Hamlet—was going to have us killed?
Why would he do that? What did we do to wrong him?
He uncovered the truth of the letter from the King you two bore.
It asked for his execution.
What? Truly?
But I didn't know that! The letter was sealed, after all...
Hamlet. Let him go.
Heh heh heh. You must think me a fool. You'd run ashore an' keep runnin' until you were clear of me!
... Not quite. However haphazard the circumstances may have been, Hamlet's uncle will be glad to have him dead.
H-he was ready to kill us. He'd gone completely mad.
So the reward won't come from us, but rather, from King Claudius.
Sounds like a lopsided trade to me.
Hamlet. Stand down. Please.
...Apologies, Ophelia.
I'll kill you too. Gladly.
I can out-fight yeh with one arm, boy.
Is that a bet you're willing to take?
...Yer more than you seem.
But not more than I.
(Damn it...)
Seems we've both got collateral to make a trade, Prince Hamlet.
Release my lieutenant, an' I won't kill yer friends. Or you.
Then we can proceed to Ireland in peace, with you in the hold.
...Now's your chance, Lady Grace.
He won't come easily.
W...what? What's going on?
We were alerted to your plan, Hamlet. You uncouth, lackless, friendless fool.
Yer ladies here have struck a bargain. They've offered me gold for yer head.
A-ah... no...
Now, ladies. As to the matter of yer payment.
I...It'll be arranged upon arrival at Denmark.
...Well, well. Time for the masks t'come off.
Well played, everyone.
Ophelia told all of us about your plans.
Women talk, you know!
Why? Why would you tell them?
Yes, what on earth is happening?
Heard about yer little plan to overthrow me, Princey.
Luckily, yer lass Ophelia here tipped me off ahead o' time.
A mutiny?
Ergh. Why would you betray my confidence, Ophelia?
You plotting bitch. Canna' believe I fell for it.
I have to keep my friends alive first.
And if I refuse to give in?
...Ophelia. Is 'e always like this?
Release myself and Lady Ophelia in a longboat close to Danish shores. You can keep the ship and all within it.
For no further cost, you can have a new vessel. You're a sharp woman. You see the value in such a trade, don't you?
We're no good to you as a ransom. A mad prince set for slaughter—who would pay for me?
Now yer speakin' a common tongue.
Very well, Prince Hamlet. You've proved your mettle.
I'll return you an' your lady-love to Denmark.
Mercy is a gift I don't often grant.
Yeh are well and truly mad.
So they say.
This is why I hate yeh all, the courtly, crowned lot. All yeh do is murder one another.
Yeh speak so prettily. And it all amounts to nothin'.
One day yer family, the next yer at each other's throats. Out here on the sea, I trust my crew more'n any one of you.
I'd kill yeh all outright, but seein' as Ophelia here saw fit t'warn me in advance...
I'll be takin' this ship as my prize, an' I'll leave yeh on Danish shores.
An' clean up this blood in the meantime, too. Stains the wood.
...That letter. The one my uncle gave you.
Inside, I found a warrant for my own death—orders for me to be executed upon arrival in England.
I trusted you both.
We didn't know about the contents of the letter. I swear to you, Hamlet.
If we thought we were delivering something like that...
Certainly, there are far less convoluted ways to murder someone.
My thoughts exactly! Like pushing Hamlet overboard and making it look like an accident!
Or staging an attack on the ship!
Or poisoning his dinner...
What about strangling him in his sleep?
Are you idiots done?
Oh, I suppose. Just sort of lost in thought, there. Where were we?
Despite promising Ophelia I wouldn't hurt you lot, I find myself reconsiderin'.
Maybe I'll just take a coupla hands off.
Grace. Please don't.
Wot? Still aching for his sword?
You can't harm him. He's important to me, and to his country.
Not even a little slice? What about a thumb? Surely he can get by with just one thumb up his arse.
Not even a thumb.
I resent that statement.
I didn't ask yeh, Royal Pain.
It appears my three companions have their own stones to cast at one another.
Uh, yes! What she said!
We apologize so very humbly for this inconvenient disturbance, your pirate ladyship.
Additionally, please don't kill us.
Yer lucky to owe yer life to this woman, Prince.
She's at least got a drop of integrity. The rest of yeh, not so much.
I'll return you all to Denmark.
Mercy is a gift I don't often grant. Yer all fortunate today.
Mercy means returning to Elsinore? Certainly doesn't feel that way.
Back we go, then.
We've arrived. This ship and all her wares are mine now. On yer way, now!
So it's true. I'd heard you returned.
And so has Hamlet, looking the picture of health.
I put my faith in you. I won't make a mistake like that again.
And my idiot nephew is 'handled' at last. I'm impressed; you've done exactly what I needed of you.
It appears you are quite a whit more cunning than you seem.
You have my thanks, and my gratitude.
You're as clever as you are beautiful.
I aim to please.
My sweet. The time has come. Are you prepared to announce our news?
This is all happening so fast.
These things tend to.
I shall announce some news without further ado.
Lady Ophelia and I are to be betrothed. Today.
A-ah... why hadn't I heard of this?
Never mind it... yes, never mind it.
My lord, are you sure you don't want to wait for the castle chaplain to return from his countryside tour?
Absolutely certain, Bernardo. We shan't wait another minute.
A-and—Lady Ophelia—this is your desire as well? This union?
It is rather, er, surprising, given the circumstances.
I know it's sudden, Bernardo. But it's what I want. Truly.
Let us all bear witness to the betrothal of His Majesty Claudius of Denmark, and Lady Ophelia, daughter of Duke Polonius.
As Bernardo is elsewhere, I'd like to request that Voltemand here do the honors.
